title: Fabrication of Three-dimensional Paper-based Microfluidic Devices for Immunoassays
protocol: Prepare patterns for layers of paper, nylon, and adhesive using graphic design software.
Spray the work area with a solution of 70% ethanol and water.
Wipe the work area with a clean paper towel.
Cut a stock sheet of paper into standard paper size using a large tabletop paper cutter.
Handle paper with clean gloves to minimize contamination.
Load a cut sheet of chromatography paper into the printer tray.
Print previously designed layers.
Cut the stock roll of nylon membrane into sheets (7.5 x 10 inches) using a tabletop paper cutter.
Handle the cut nylon membrane carefully to maintain its integrity and prevent ripping.
Store any unused nylon membrane in a desiccator cabinet.
Print a capture layer pattern onto a piece of copy paper using a wax printer.
Tape the printed sheet of copy paper to a light box as a guide for positioning.
Place a clean sheet of copy paper on top of the printed sheet on the light box.
Tape the clean sheet of copy paper to the light box, but do not tape it to the printed layer.
Place a cut sheet of nylon membrane onto the clean piece of copy paper.
Ensure that the nylon membrane covers the printed area of the bottom layer of copy paper.
Tape all four sides of the nylon membrane securely to the clean sheet of copy paper.
Load a sheet of nylon membrane supported by copy paper into the manual feed printer tray.
Tape the printed layers onto an acrylic frame for even heating above and below the layer when placed in a gravity convection oven.
Keep the nylon membrane taped to the support sheet of copy paper until after the wax is melted and hydrophobic barriers are formed.
Place the layers in the oven at 150 °C for 30 sec until the wax melts into the thickness of the paper.
Confirm that the wax has permeated the thickness of the paper by turning it over and checking for imperfections in the design.
Remove the paper and nylon membrane from the acrylic frame.
Remove nylon membrane from support sheet of copy paper.
Pattern double-sided sheets of adhesive films using a robotic knife plotter, using design files previously prepared.
Protect any exposed adhesive surface using a sheet of wax liner.
Spray the light box with a solution of 70% (v/v) ethanol and water.
Wipe the light box with a clean paper towel.
Tape a patterned layer of paper or nylon membrane onto the light box with the printed side down.
Peel one side of protective liner from the patterned sheet of adhesive and affix it to the layer of paper or nylon membrane.
Press together using the light box for proper alignment.
Place the partially assembled device into a protective slip.
Pass the two-layer assembly through an automated laminator.
Tape conjugate layer onto an acrylic frame such that the hydrophilic zone is suspended and not in contact with the frame.
Add 2.5 µl of 100 mg/ml bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the hydrophilic zone on the conjugate layer.
Allow it to dry at room temperature for 2 min.
Dry at 65 °C for 5 min.
Add 5 µl of 5 O.D. colloidal gold nanoparticle conjugated to anti-β-hCG antibody to the hydrophilic zone.
Repeat the drying process (2 min at room temperature and then at 65 °C for 5 min).
Tape lateral channel layer onto an acrylic frame such that the hydrophilic zone is suspended and not in contact with the frame.
Add 10 µl of blocking agent (5 mg/ml non-fat milk and 0.1% (v/v) Tween 20 in 1x PBS) to treat the lateral channel.
Allow it to dry at room temperature for 2 min.
Dry at 65 °C for 5 min.
Tape the hydrophilic zone of the capture layer onto an acrylic frame without contact with the frame.
Treat the capture layer with 5 µL of 1 mg/ml anti-α-hCG antibody.
Allow the treated sample to dry at room temperature for 2 min.
Dry the sample further at 65 °C for 8 min.
Add 2 µL of blocking agent (5 mg/ml non-fat milk and 0.1% (v/v) Tween 20 in 1x PBS).
Repeat the drying process for the capture layer.
Tape the wash layer to the light box with the printed side facing upwards.
Remove alignment holes from subsequent layers using a handheld hole-punch tool if necessary.
Expose the adhesive on the back of the capture layer by removing its protective film.
Align the capture layer above the wash layer using the alignment holes as a guide.
Press the two layers together, avoiding touching hydrophilic zones to minimize contamination or damage.
Expose the adhesive on the back of the incubation layer by removing its protective film.
Align the incubation layer above the capture layer and press them together.
Continue adding layers in this manner until all active layers are assembled.
Place the partially assembled device into a protective slip and firmly affix the layers together using a laminator.
Remove the protective film on the back of the wash layer and affix the blot layer to the bottom of the device.
Repeat lamination step to complete the assembly of the three-dimensional paper-based microfluidic device.
Cut desired number of devices from strips or sheets of fully-assembled devices using scissors.
Add 20 µl of a sample to the hydrophilic zone on top of the device (i.e., the sample layer).
Wait for the sample to wick completely into the device, then add 15 µl of wash buffer (0.05% v/v Tween 20 in 1x phosphate buffered saline).
After the first aliquot of wash buffer has wicked completely into the device, add a second 15 µl aliquot of wash buffer.
Peel away the three top layers of the device using tweezers to expose the capture layer.
Interpret the results of the assay qualitatively by observing the presence or absence of color.
Image the readout layer using a desktop scanner.
Use image processing software or algorithms to quantify results and characterize the distributions of intensity within a detection zone.
